activities.title: Push the piles together
activities.intro: Two little groups are going to become one big group. Push them together with your eyes, count everything, then tap how many.
activities.offScreen: Put 2 spoons and 3 spoons together on the table, push them into one pile, and count how many altogether.

rounds.prompt: 2 red fish swim over to 2 blue fish. How many fish altogether? Touch each one as you count, then tap the number.
2 green leaves land next to 3 yellow leaves. How many leaves altogether? Count them all, then tap the number.
3 blue blocks meet 3 red blocks. How many blocks altogether? Touch each one as you count, then tap the number.
2 purple flowers grow next to 4 orange flowers. How many flowers altogether? Count them all, then tap the number.

activities.title: Tower math
activities.intro: A little tower joins a big tower. Count all the blocks in the new tall tower, then tap how many.
activities.offScreen: Build a 2-block tower and a 3-block tower, stack them into one tower, and count the new tower from the bottom.

rounds.prompt: A tower of 2 red blocks lands on a tower of 3 blue blocks. How many blocks in the new tower? Count every block, then tap the number.
A tower of 3 red blocks lands on a tower of 3 blue blocks. How many blocks in the new tower? Count every block, then tap the number.
A tower of 3 green blocks lands on a tower of 4 yellow blocks. How many blocks in the new tower? Count every block, then tap the number.
A tower of 4 red blocks lands on a tower of 4 blue blocks. How many blocks in the new tower? Count every block, then tap the number.

activities.title: One more joins
activities.intro: Everyone is here, and then one more friend arrives. Count again after the new friend joins, then tap how many.
activities.offScreen: Line up 4 toys, let one more toy join the line, and count the whole line again.

rounds.prompt: 3 brown birds sit on the branch and 1 orange bird flies in. How many birds now? Touch each one as you count, then tap the number.
4 blue fish are swimming and 1 orange fish joins them. How many fish now? Count them all, then tap the number.
5 yellow stars are shining and 1 purple star pops up. How many stars now? Touch each one as you count, then tap the number.

parentCard.title: Tower math
steps: Build a tower of 2 blocks and a tower of 3 blocks together, and count each tower out loud.
Ask them how many blocks the two towers will make together, and let them guess before anything moves.
Stack them into one tower and count it from the bottom, one number for one block.
Play again with 3 and 3, then 4 and 4 if the counting stays strong, and let them build the towers themselves.
notice: When the towers join, do they count the new tower from 1, or count on from the tower they already counted?
Do their guesses before the stack get closer as the game goes on?
Do they still say exactly one number for one block, even past 5?
